title: Release Traffic Quickstart Snapshot Pack: compact canary, A/B and fallback walkthrough assets
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, copy-light quickstart snapshot pack for the Release Traffic feature that covers: 1) canary deployments with traffic split visualization, 2) A/B variant setup and comparison card, and 3) automated fallback policy flow. Deliver annotated product screenshots, responsive variants (desktop and narrow sidebar), and export-ready assets for docs and the in-console guided tour.
acceptance_criteria: One desktop and one narrow-width variant for each walkthrough step (total 6 screenshots) exported at 2x and 3x
Annotations and callouts in separate layer groups (Figma) so engineering can toggle overlays
Copy approved by PM and legal for all CTA/button text
WCAG 2.1 AA contrast checks for all UI callouts and overlays
Variant comparison card demonstrates latency/cost knobs and a clear pin/unpin affordance
comments: 2026-03-10 MC: Initial kickoff. Scoped 6 primary shots: canary intro, canary traffic editor, A/B create flow, A/B compare card, fallback policy dialog, fallback autoswitch success state.
2026-03-11 AR: First-pass mocks uploaded to Figma. Chose compact cards over full-page walkthrough to reduce cognitive load for new users.
2026-03-12 PM (Daniel Ortiz): Prefer explicit cost callout on the A/B compare card. Requesting copy change: 'Estimated token cost per 1k requests' instead of 'Cost estimate'.

2026-03-12 ENG (Lina Park): Need to ensure the traffic heatmap uses telemetry-safe synthetic data and does not leak customer IDs. Also suggested adding a collapsed advanced link for sample rate controls.
2026-03-13 MC: Updated contrast and annotated overlays. Ran WCAG checks and increased border weight on selected variant to meet AA contrast.
2026-03-14 AR: Ready for review. Exported 2x assets in the Drive folder and added layer naming convention doc. Leaving for design review and PM signoff.
review_feedback: PM Daniel: Move cost callout to top-right of compare card and use a tooltip for methodology.
Eng Lina: Make sure the fallback dialog clearly lists fallback model variant rules and shows a simulated latency impact line (mocked).
Security (Alex M): Confirm no real customer telemetry in screenshots; please use seeded demo namespace 'acme-demo'.
Design Lead (Ravi S): Good compact layout. Suggest adding an accessible focus outline for keyboard walkthrough steps.
decisions: Use compact modal + inline card pattern rather than full-screen tour to reduce setup friction
Render a simplified synthetic heatmap for traffic distribution instead of raw telemetry
Include both desktop (1200px) and narrow (360px) variants to cover Console and embedded quickstarts
Annotate callouts as separate Figma frames so docs team can toggle annotations on/off
next_steps: Address Eng note: add 'advanced sample rate' collapsed control by 2026-03-18
Legal to sign off on demo namespace and screenshots by 2026-03-18
Publish exported assets to docs repo and link in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/3124 after approvals
screenshots_needed: Canary overview with 10% traffic split highlighted
Canary traffic editor with split slider and confirmation CTA
A/B variant creation modal showing model pin toggle
A/B compare card with latency and cost callouts
Fallback policy dialog with autoswitch toggle and reason codes
Fallback success toast and automatic reroute visualization
designer_notes: Aim for a single-screen narrative per concept — quick comprehension on first glance. Avoid technical jargon on initial cards; surface latency and cost as simple numbers with tooltips. Keep overlays opt-in for the docs page to allow code screenshots to remain clean.
localization_notes: Reserve 20% extra width for German copy on primary CTA buttons
Provide a no-text icon-only variant for narrow layouts where translations will be applied by i18n team
